chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) performed the Aqeeqa for Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) with his own hand and said: 'In the Name of Allah, an Aqeeqa for Al-Hasan.' And he said: 'O Allah, its bone with his bone, its flesh with his flesh, its blood with his blood, and its hair with his hair. O Allah, make it a shield for Muhammad and his Progeny.'

key_terms.عَقَّ: Performed the ritual sacrifice of Aqeeqa
key_terms.عَقِيقَةٌ: Aqeeqa, the ritual sacrifice offered for a newborn child

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Prophet's Aqeeqa for Al-Hasan and the associated supplication?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the Prophet Muhammad’s personal involvement in the Aqeeqa ritual for Al-Hasan, emphasizing the spiritual significance of the sacrifice as a protective shield (wiqa') for the Ahl al-Bayt. The supplication linking the animal's physical attributes to the Imam reflects the Shia belief in the metaphysical connection between the Imams and divine protection, a concept rooted in the tradition of the Prophet and the Imams. This practice underscores the importance of Aqeeqa not merely as a cultural custom but as a sacred act of devotion and intercession.
